subject: sociology
title: Who Really Rules?
welcome_lead: Pluralists, elitists and Marxists each say someone different runs the show. Time to apply the theories.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying pluralism, elite theory and Marxism to who holds political power.
final_note: Always name the perspective, the thinker, and a current British example.

concepts.def: Power is shared among many competing groups.
Pareto, Mosca: a small minority always rules.
Marxist: the bourgeoisie holds real political power.
Michels: even democratic groups grow elites.

walkthroughs.body_html: Pluralists like Robert Dahl argue power is spread. Unions, charities, businesses and protest groups all compete for influence. Voting and pressure groups keep the system responsive.

Elite theorists say every society is ruled by a minority. Pareto called this the 'circulation of elites'. Even revolutions just replace one elite with another. Michels added the iron law of oligarchy.
Marxists argue democracy is a façade. The state serves the ruling class: corporate donors, media owners and 'revolving door' policymakers shape laws to protect profit.
